title: Find the file
summary: Navigate a filesystem and locate the file that holds store inventory.

scenario.briefing: The server room files are organized in folders. Find the live inventory file without opening unrelated data or backups.

objectives.description: Check understanding through the remaining explanation and transfer evidence.

hints: Open srv, then campus. The application files live under srv/campus.
Data and logs are separate folders under srv/campus.
The file is named inventory.json and sits in the data folder.
Navigate srv, campus, data, then select inventory.json.

misconceptions.description: Selecting an old backup instead of the live file.
misconceptions.feedback: The backup is not the file the running service uses. Live data is in srv/campus/data.
.. moves up one folder. From app, ../data means go up to campus, then into data.

misconceptions.description: Assuming a file extension guarantees valid content.
misconceptions.feedback: An extension is a naming convention. A .json file can contain invalid JSON or something else entirely.

sections.title: Folders are named containers
sections.body: A filesystem organizes files in a tree. An absolute path starts at the root, such as /srv/campus/data/inventory.json. A relative path starts from the current folder. Both can identify the same file.

sections.title: Names are not locations
sections.body: Two folders can contain files with the same name. The complete path and the current working directory determine which file a program opens. Selecting an old backup by mistake can make a service read stale data.

vocabulary.definition: A folder that contains files or other folders.
A path that starts at the filesystem root.
A path interpreted from the current directory.

hints: Open the folders and choose the live inventory file, not a copy.
A path identifies a file by its folder chain; similar names in backups are different files.
In /home/student/notes.txt the folders are home and student and the file is notes.txt.
The live data sits beside orders.json under campus, not under backups. Navigate there and select it.
steps.title: Locate inventory.json
steps.prompt: Navigate the folders and select the live inventory file. Do not select a backup.
steps.explanation: The live inventory file is srv/campus/data/inventory.json. The similarly named file in backups is stale.

steps.title: Read the relative path
steps.prompt: Your current directory is /srv/campus/app. Which path opens the live inventory file?

quiz.explanation: From app, .. moves up to campus. Then data/inventory.json reaches the live file.

hints: Start at /srv/campus/app and find the shortest correct relative path.
.. moves up one folder; a name without .. moves down from the current folder.
You need to leave app first, then enter data. Build the path from that move.
Select statements that are true about how paths and files behave.
Names are scoped by folders, relative paths depend on the current directory, and extensions are conventions.
Two files named config.json can exist in different folders without conflict.
Two statements are accurate; reject the claims about backups being live and extensions proving content.
steps.title: Paths and identity

statements.label: Two different files can share a file name in different folders.
A relative path depends on the current directory.
A backup file is always the live data source.
A .json extension guarantees the file is valid JSON.

steps.explanation: Paths disambiguate names. Extensions and folder names are conventions, not proof of content.

accessibility.summary: The filesystem is a keyboard-navigable tree with expandable folders. A breadcrumb shows the current path.
accessibility.keyboardNotes: Use arrow keys to move through the tree and Enter to open a folder or select a file.
accessibility.screenReaderNotes: Each folder announces expanded or collapsed state. The breadcrumb and selected file are read as text.
